subject: Custodian responsibilities and cross-border access controls for private installs
messages:
From: Lucia Morales <privacy@medsphere.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: daniel.connors@medsphere.com
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment – operator access / key custody clarifications

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we prepare the internal procurement packet for a private VPC install of Redwood, the legal and security teams have a few open items we need clarified so we can finalize the DPA and SOW. High level questions:

- Will Redwood ever have access to plaintext customer data for private VPC/on‑prem installs if the customer holds the encryption keys? If yes, under what operational scenarios (debugging, emergency support, subpoena)?
- We need a precise list of subprocessors and whether any of them will have access to decrypted data in private deployments.
- How does Redwood handle operator break‑glass and remote troubleshooting? Is there a documented access workflow and logging that we can surface in the contract?
- Cross‑border transfers: our systems are EU‑based; we need to understand whether any logs, telemetry, or backups will leave the EU when using Redwood support channels.

Can you send a short written summary and any recommended DPA language we can propose to Procurement? If possible attach an operator access flow diagram and a matrix showing which roles may see keys or decrypted material.

Appreciate it — we’re trying to hit an internal December 1 signoff.

– Lucia
Privacy & Procurement, Medsphere Health

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Lucia Morales <privacy@medsphere.com>, Daniel Connors <daniel.connors@medsphere.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2025 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment – operator access / key custody clarifications

Hi Lucia (and Daniel),

Thanks for the clear list — here are concise answers and a proposed contract approach. Attaching a brief KMS custody matrix and an operator access flowchart. I’ll also include a sample DPA clause in a follow up reply with Laura’s redlines.

Summary answers (short):
- Customer‑managed keys (BYOK) option: when customers provide and manage their own KMS keys (cloud KMS or on‑prem HSM), Redwood does not persist plaintext customer data in our control plane. Operator access to decrypted data is blocked by design unless the customer explicitly enables an application‑level support session.
- Support/debugging flow: Redwood can request a time‑bounded support session that the customer explicitly authorizes (one‑time session tokens + audit logs). When authorized, a limited‑scope Redwood engineer session may access application logs; at no point do we require customers to hand over root KMS keys.
- Subprocessors: for private installs the list is heavily constrained. The only subprocessors that may be involved in support workflows are our managed observability partner and a limited set of infrastructure vendors; neither has access to decrypted customer payloads when BYOK is in use. Full list attached.
- Cross‑border: by default we keep audit logs and telemetry within the region indicated on the SOW. For EU installations we operate a region‑restricted telemetry pipeline; any exception requires explicit written consent and will appear in the SOW.

Recommended contract language (brief):
- "Customer retains sole custody of encryption keys for BYOK deployments. Redwood shall not access plaintext customer data except when explicitly authorized by the customer through documented session authorization flows. Any exception will be limited in scope and time and will be subject to the audit logging and notification requirements herein."

Next steps: Laura will send a redline for the DPA paragraph and Marcus will follow up on operator break‑glass safeguards and logging retention. Happy to set a technical conversation with your engineering team this week.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Security & Compliance (GTMs)
Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Lucia Morales <privacy@medsphere.com>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 08:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment – operator access / key custody clarifications

Lucia — I’m attaching a proposed DPA redline (dpa-redline-proposal.docx) but here are the key contractual bullets we think will close this quickly: 

1) Key custody clause: "Customer is the sole controller of Customer Keys. Redwood will implement technical controls to prevent the decryption of Customer Data unless Customer grants explicit, auditable, time‑limited access for the purpose of troubleshooting. Redwood shall not require transfer of Customer Keys as a precondition to support."

2) Access authorization: require SAML/OAuth identity assertions from the customer for any support session plus a one‑time token tied to a ticket number (this prevents password transfer).

3) Subprocessor covenant: list all potential subprocessors and include a carve‑out stating "no subprocessor will have the ability to access decrypted Customer Data in BYOK configurations."

4) Escrow/escrow for legal requests: propose language that Redwood will notify the customer and provide metadata of requests; Redwood will refuse disclosure of plaintext unless compelled by a lawful order and only after notifying the customer and providing a copy where permitted.

Let us know if Medsphere legal wants stronger notification windows (we can do 48 hours notice where permitted).

—Laura
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, lucia.morales@medsphere.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment – operator access / key custody clarifications

Adding ops notes re: remote troubleshooting and break‑glass: 

- For VPC installs we recommend a dedicated bastion/jump host that the customer controls. Redwood engineers request ephemeral access via the customer portal; the customer opens a time‑boxed window and provides an ephemeral SSH key scoped to the jump host.
- If customers prefer a managed option, we can operate a customer‑managed transit VPN that terminates inside the customer network; Redwood never bridges into the customer network without a ticket and explicit approval.
- Audit trail: every support session will generate immutable logs (session start/end, commands run, file access patterns). We retain telemetry for 90 days by default; longer retention can be negotiated.
- Operator break‑glass: documented runbook — must include: justification, ticket id, customer approval token, and email notification to security and the named customer contact. We can include a clause that any break‑glass access be certified quarterly by a third party for high‑sensitivity customers.

Attachment: operator-access-flowchart.png (flow and required approvals).

—Sergio
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: Lucia Morales <privacy@medsphere.com>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 14:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment – operator access / key custody clarifications

Lucia — quick operational clarifications and a proposed acceptance checklist for the SOW: 

1) BYOK verification: before go‑live we perform a non‑destructive key handshake test (customer signs a nonce) to prove key control without exposing plaintext.
2) Logging & backups: backups are encrypted with customer keys when BYOK is enabled. Service metadata required for operation (metrics, task queues) are collected in region and do not contain unencrypted customer payloads.
3) Subprocessor list and attestations: we will provide an enumerated list and SOC2 statements for each subprocessors involved in the install; any change that would give a subprocessor access to decrypted data will require a prior written amendment.

If Medsphere is OK with those points I recommend we 1) finalize the DPA redline, 2) sign an SOW that includes the acceptance checklist above, and 3) set a short technical call for permissioned session walkthrough (we can do Wed or Thu morning PST).

Thanks — I’ll stand by for calendar times.

—Marcus
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
